correctness.rationale: Antipodal parity reduces evaluation of H_l on 24 symmetric vertices to a 12×12 positive-semidefinite Legendre Gram G_l=P_l(<xi,xj>). Reconstructed the regular vertex coordinates and independently computed modular ranks over F_998244353 for every l=0..115: 1,3,5,7,9,11 for l<=5; 12 for l=6,7,8; rank10 at l=9; 12 for l=10..115. Independently evaluated P9 in Q(sqrt2) and verified two linearly independent null relations u1−u2,u1−u3, proving the matching rank-10 upper bound and the two signed block constraints. Prime modulus has certified square-root of 2 and invertible recurrence denominators, so nonzero modular minors prove characteristic-zero lower bounds. Off-diagonal |<xi,xj>|≤(7+4sqrt2)/17 with sqrt(1−t²)>2/3; the classical Bernstein Legendre inequality makes the sum of 11 off-diagonal magnitudes <1 from l=116 onward, forcing full rank by strict diagonal dominance. A nonzero rank-12 modular witness at deformation b=2 makes the degree-nine Gram determinant a nonidentically-zero analytic function of b; hence the regular zero is isolated. Finite arithmetic and analytic tail are both indispensable.
